# IEC 60601-1-8 — Medical electrical equipment — Part 1-8: General requirements, tests and guidance for alarm systems

_Demo sample data — not for clinical use._

**Standard**: IEC 60601-1-8:2006 + AMD1:2012 + AMD2:2020 (Edition 2.2, consolidated version, 2020-07) — the FDA-recognized edition (Recognition Number 5-131, Extent: Complete)
**Category**: Medical electrical equipment — alarm systems (collateral standard to IEC 60601-1)
**Registry distillation (L1a)**: [`.claude/skills/medtech-docs/references/standards/iec-60601-1-8.md`](../../../.claude/skills/medtech-docs/references/standards/iec-60601-1-8.md) — clause-level finding aid; carries the 🔎 non-authoritative banner and `[VERIFY]` marks
**Module Applicability**: PP3500 alarm subsystem — pump firmware alarm-priority engine, audio driver, speaker/annunciator hardware, and user-facing visual alarm indicators
**Original Source**: [webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/67388](https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/67388)

## Overview

IEC 60601-1-8 specifies basic safety and essential performance requirements for alarm systems in medical electrical equipment — alarm categories (priorities) by degree of urgency, consistent alarm signals, and consistent control states and their marking. It applies to the PP3500 because the device annunciates alarm conditions (e.g., occlusion, air-in-line) through an audible high/medium/low-priority alarm scheme plus visual annunciation, and alarm integrity is safety-critical: a silent or unheard alarm leaves the underlying hazardous situation uncorrected.

This file records **project applicability only**. For what the standard says, consult the L1a registry distillation linked above — and note that the distillation is a finding aid: clause-level content not verified there requires the licensed standard itself.

## PP3500 Applicability

### Design input — DI-019

`docs/project/dhfs/pca-device/design-controls/requirements/design-inputs.md` DI-019 (G3, INTE, **CTF**): the device shall provide audible alarms compliant with IEC 60601-1-8 for high-, medium-, and low-priority alarm categories, with sound pressure level adjustable from 45 to 80 dB(A) at 1 m. Traces up to UN-010 and decomposes into SW-012 (alarm-priority engine routes alarm events to the audio driver with priority melodies and per-priority SPL mixing).

### Risk file linkage

- **HAZ-008** (`docs/project/dhfs/pca-device/risk-management/GL-TMP-RM-003-hazard-analysis.md`) — "Alarm failure — not annunciated or not heard": alarm condition exists but staff are not alerted (speaker fault, or SPL inadequate for ward noise). Risk control is the IEC 60601-1-8-compliant priority alarm scheme with adjustable SPL (DI-019, protective) plus IEC 60601-1 / IEC 60601-2-24 essential-performance compliance (DI-010). Residual risk ALARP. The row also carries an **alarm-fatigue side-assessment**: high SPL settings contribute to alarm fatigue, assessed S2/P3 = Acceptable per GL-STD-RM-001 §5 (new-risk-from-risk-control evaluation).
- **FM-D-018** (`docs/project/dhfs/pca-device/risk-management/GL-TMP-RM-004-design-fmea.md`) — speaker/annunciator audible-alarm-output failure mode (speaker open, amp fault → no sound pressure). Prevention control: alarm system qualified to the IEC 60601-1-8 SPL range 45–80 dB(A) (DI-019). Detection controls: power-on speaker self-test with fault annunciation; alarm events mirrored to EHR (DI-023). Links to HAZ-008.

### Verification approach

Per DI-019 / HAZ-008: **acoustic measurement in an anechoic chamber** — verify the SPL adjustment range and alarm-melody compliance for all three alarm categories (bench test), alongside third-party safety testing per IEC 60601-1 / IEC 60601-2-24 covering alarm-function integrity.
